President Trump said Sunday, Nov. 22, that he is inclined to resume military strikes on Iran after the new year if the two countries fail to reach an agreement, according to exclusive comments to Fox News. Trump said indirect talks with Tehran are continuing but called Iranian negotiators "professional tap dancers" who "talk all the time," and said Iran is "more aggressive now than before the election." Asked about Iranian state media reports that Iran could test the U.S. naval blockade of its ports, he said: "I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy." He also urged anti-government protesters in Iran to "keep protesting." On Truth Social, Trump wrote that Iran "has launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year" and that all were knocked down without damage. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they struck U.S. Patriot radars in Bahrain on Saturday; Bahrain says a civilian industrial facility was hit and two people were injured, and a U.S. official told CBS News there was no damage to U.S. forces. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said "the window of diplomacy is still open" but Iran is ready for any scenario. Bloomberg reported that Britain and several Gulf states have privately urged Washington not to launch new strikes. Incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries called the conflict a "reckless and costly war of choice" that has raised gas prices. Sources: Fox News, Anadolu Agency, Iran International, CBS News.
